reason: The junctions appear suited to joining the surface cells into a more continuous barrier.
expectation: The cells will form a joined surface layer that helps limit water loss.

effect: The junctions hold the surface cells together, but water still escapes from the exposed sheet. The outer layer looks like the next part of the barrier.
reaction: The water loss makes the need for another layer clear.
reason: The tough outer layer has overlapping cells and lipids that appear suited to covering the exposed surface.
expectation: The outer layer will cover the connected cells and reduce water loss.

effect: The outer layer reduced water loss, leaving support and sensing to build.
reaction: The comparison makes the barrier's role clear.
reason: The connective fibers and skin support cells appear to form the supporting tissue beneath the surface.
expectation: They will form a supportive skin layer.

effect: The fibers and support cells formed a layer that resists a sideways tug and includes capillaries. It appears ready to support the surface barrier.
reaction: The tug panels make the fibers’ supporting role clear.
reason: The supporting layer and surface barrier look like complementary parts of the skin.
expectation: They will form a layered skin structure with support beneath the water-loss barrier.

effect: The supporting layer and surface barrier formed layered skin, with nutrients reaching living surface cells from vessels below. The skin still needs sensory endings.
reaction: The cross-section clearly connects the skin layers to their blood supply.
reason: The sensory endings belong beneath the skin surface and should let it detect contact.
expectation: The skin will gain a way to sense touch.

effect: The skin can now sense contact as well as limit water loss. The next goal is to connect it and the supply network to the arm.
reaction: The fingertip picture makes the sensory endings’ role clear.
reason: The sensitive skin should cover and protect the working arm.
expectation: The arm will gain a protective, touch-sensitive covering.

effect: The skin now covers the arm and connects to its nerves; the open vessels still need the body supply network.
reaction: The open vessel ends make the next connection clear.
reason: The body supply network can connect to the arm’s waiting vessels.
expectation: The arm will receive a continuing supply of oxygen and nutrients through its vessels.

effect: The arm is now connected to the body’s supply network, and the remaining goal is to hold the glass using contact feedback.
reaction: The new goal gives the assembled systems a concrete task.
reason: The glass is the object the living body model needs to hold.
expectation: The hand will use touch feedback to hold the glass steady.

effect: The glass sequence shows how touch feedback can guide muscle action to correct slipping, completing the chapter’s goal.
reaction: The slipping glass made the role of feedback concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass was the most worthwhile passage: it brought touch, nerves and muscles together in an everyday task, with a clear reason to adjust the grip.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the supporting layer to the surface barrier was straightforward, though its cross-section usefully showed nutrients reaching the living surface cells.

surprise.text: The connected surface sheet still lost water; adding the outer layer reduced the loss without making it completely waterproof.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt particularly arbitrary. The item names and descriptions made their intended roles reasonably clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if another chapter offered a similarly concrete problem. The glass sequence made the assembled systems more interesting than simply completing the structure.
